module_title: Union & States Articles - Law Officers, Finances, and Ordinances
introduction: At this level, we dive into the specific functional articles comparing the Union and the States. This covers the highest law officers, the financial procedures (Budgets and Money Bills), and the extraordinary ordinance-making powers of the executive.

core_concepts.title: Top Law Officers (Art 76 & 165)
core_concepts.description: Article 76 establishes the Attorney General for India (appointed by President). Using the +89 rule, Article 165 establishes the Advocate General for the State (appointed by Governor).

core_concepts.title: Pardoning Powers (Art 72 & 161)
core_concepts.description: Article 72 grants the President the power to pardon, commute, or remit sentences (including death sentences). Article 161 grants similar powers to the Governor (excluding death sentences and court-martials).

core_concepts.title: Ordinance Making Powers (Art 123 & 213)
core_concepts.description: Article 123 allows the President to promulgate Ordinances during the recess of Parliament. Article 213 allows the Governor to do the same when the state legislature is not in session.

core_concepts.title: Money Bills (Art 110 & 199)
core_concepts.description: Article 110 defines a 'Money Bill' at the Union level. Article 199 defines it at the State level. The decision of the Speaker (of Lok Sabha or Vidhan Sabha) is final in this regard.

core_concepts.title: Annual Financial Statement (Budget) (Art 112 & 202)
core_concepts.description: The term 'Budget' is not in the Constitution. Article 112 refers to the Union Budget as the 'Annual Financial Statement'. Article 202 does the same for the State Budget.

important_entities.name: Joint Sitting (Article 108)
important_entities.significance: Article 108 allows the President to summon a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament to resolve a legislative deadlock. There is NO corresponding article for states because states do not have joint sittings.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The +89 rule works perfectly up to Article 111. From Article 112 onwards, you generally need to add 90 to get the state equivalent (e.g., Union Budget Art 112 + 90 = State Budget Art 202).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: President's ordinance power is Art 123. Just swap the first two numbers (213) to get the Governor's ordinance power.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct matching questions frequently ask you to pair Article 76 (Attorney General) and Article 148 (CAG). Do not confuse the two.
Remember that the word 'Budget' is explicitly missing from the Constitution; the exam will test you on the phrase 'Annual Financial Statement' (Art 112).
